children: SKC's closure of its copper-foil production lines in South Korea as part of a restructuring is likely to trigger one-off charges in 2H, say Daiwa Capital's Henny Jung and Yoonki Bae. The analysts expect charges related to scrapping work-in-process materials and workforce restructuring to weigh on the South Korean industrial-film maker's near-term earnings. They project operating losses of 46 billion won in 3Q and 17 billion won in 4Q. The restructuring, aimed at consolidating production in lower-cost Malaysian operations, however, could help narrow losses in 1H 2027, they say. They forecast a return to operating profit in 2H 2027. Daiwa upgrades the stock to buy from hold while trimming its target price to 120,000 won from 130,000 won. Shares are 0.1% lower at 93,200 won. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
